preconditions.description: The number of cities n and roads m must satisfy 2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5 and n-1 ≤ m ≤ 10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n and 1 <= int(y) <= n and x != y for x, y in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct cities within the valid range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: len(set((min(x, y), max(x, y)) for x, y in roads)) == m
preconditions.description: There is at most one road between any pair of cities.
The graph is connected, meaning there is a path between any two cities.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n-1 integers, one for each destination city except city 1.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(out) < 10**9 + 7 for out in output.split())
postconditions.description: Each output value is a non-negative integer less than 10^9 + 7.

postconditions.expression: all(min_path_number(1, i + 1, roads) % (10**9 + 7) == int(out) for i, out in enumerate(output.split()))
postconditions.description: For each destination city i+1 (i from 0 to n-2), the output is the remainder modulo 10^9 + 7 of the smallest concatenated road number sequence from city 1 to city i+1.
